prompt:
Iris…? Where are we…? Whose blood is this?
You okay?
It’ll pass.
What’s your name?
Noah.
What’s the walkie-talkie for?
Where’s your mom?
Here.
Wrap up.
I have to pay first.
Do you remember Mom?
Water. For some reason, always water.
What’s up north?
That’s not an answer.
Iris… what happened at home?
What are we going to do with him?
My head’s quiet.
Was I wrong to throw them out?
Maybe I should have taken one.
…I don’t know.
Iris… how are you holding up?
Danny, what’s she like — your mom?
Zoe, where are you even from?
Iris, where are we actually going?
What’s going on with the highway?
Is there a way around?
You coming from the north?
Two coffees. One to go — out on the porch.
I promised.
Coffee. If that’s all right.
What do we owe you?
Is it always this empty?
It’s all the same. Blizzard.
Show me.
I won’t bother you.
What are you drawing?
Your mom will find you.
We’ll tell her where you are.
I’m keeping the engine running. Or we’ll freeze.
Tell me about Grandma.
Why?
Eva, how are you doing?
A month, you said?
You said he erases people. What does that mean?
Danny, you cold?
The exhaust’s buried.
Crack the windows. Nobody sleeps.
I’ll dig it out. You can’t start it with the pipe blocked.
I’ll find the car. By feel.
Keep the window open a crack.
Was she happy?
Wait. I didn’t mean to scare you. I’m sorry.
Whose van is this?
Why didn’t you sell it?
Where are we going?
Who are you making?
Don’t go far.
Grandma… what was she like? Mom.
Danny, you doing okay back there?
Zoe, are you all right?
Iris, get some sleep. I’ll wake you.
Wait by the gate. If anyone comes — shout.
Mom…
Mom. I’ll tell you later. Let’s go.
Nothing. Let’s go.
I packed it myself. So Mom wouldn’t get mad that I was slow.
He knew where we’d be. And when.
Why did you bring me here? Honestly.
That night, at home… Was it really me?
I’m sorry. About the diary.
And after? When it’s all over?
I won’t let anyone take you.
I’m sorry. There’s nothing there.
No. No sleeping today. Sing. Anything — just sing.

Drive. North.
Fine.
Go pay. I’ll sit with him.
Pay and come straight back. Don’t talk to anyone.
Your head again?
Noah! Don’t go over there.
Noah. We need to go.
A little. Her hands. …You?
No one’s looking for us there.
It’s the only one I’ve got.
You already asked.
Not now. Please.
I don’t know. But we’re not leaving him.
You can.
Quiet isn’t the same as okay.
On them you sleep with your eyes open.
I don’t know, Noah. I really don’t.
Noah… Don’t get out. Please.
You ran from the police with kids in the car. How do you think I am?
Fine. Don’t ask, okay? Just get us there.
North. I’ll tell you the rest later. Just drive.
It’s not Mom. It’s just… a woman.
Noah. Sit down already. People are looking.
That’s the doctor’s car. Hale’s. He used to come see you.
Don’t drive. Let’s wait till it dies down.
Agnes. Mom’s mom. Dad wouldn’t even let us talk about her.
I don’t know. In the diary, Mom writes about her like she’s asking forgiveness.
I’ve never even seen her.
I don’t know.
Where are you going?
You won’t see a thing out there.
Always.
And you left?
He doesn’t.
…I remember we have to keep going.
Digging the car out.
He always comes back.
Turn it off.
How do we know she isn’t with him?
You need to see this.
You won’t. You blank out at the wheel yourself — I’ve seen it.
I’m coming with you.
Well? What’s in there?
We’ll go down there. Together. Just not yet.
You used to push me here. Higher, higher… And Mom would shout from the porch, “Easy, you two!”
You packed mine too. I remember the bunny in the pocket.
That one’s mine. I drank milk out of it. Warm, with skin on top — gross.
I thought it was a phone number.
He has the diary… Wait. There were numbers inside the cover. I thought it was a phone number.
“Not even your mother”… He made sure Grandma didn’t know either.
I remember. Why do you even care?
So you’d remember. You’re the only one who saw what happened that night. Without you, nothing happens to him.
And so you’d stop taking his pills. I want my brother back. The real one.
You stood between us. If it weren’t for you, I wouldn’t be here.
It wasn’t quite you. But it wasn’t him either. I don’t know, Noah. I really don’t.
You gave Mom to him. A second time.
You wanted him to let us go. I know. It still hurts.
They’ll send me to a children’s home. And you — back to him. Or to prison.
Grandma says I can live with her. If they let me.
I’ve read about you. In Mom’s diary.
He drowned, and you’re the one they blame. I know what really happened.

Your hands are dirty.
Danny. You?
Like in the book. With the boat and the animals.
Mom has the other one. She said: if anything happens, push and talk.
Mom. Over…
She never answers the first time.
She said: wait here, I’ll be quick.
It was still light out.
Are you leaving?
I’m not asleep. I can hear you.
Can I eat the chocolate now?
She sings when she’s nice. When she drinks, she sleeps. I left her the other walkie-talkie.
If she turns it on, she’ll find me. She always finds me.
A house. Mom. And the walkie-talkie — so she can hear.
What if we go really far?
No. Is your grandma nice?
Just so you know, I’m not scared of her.
Where’s Noah?
He won’t get lost?
Mom… I’m here…
I’m gonna go find my mom. She’s probably back at the gas station by now.
A guard. So he can watch the van while we’re gone.
I’m right here. I can see the van.
Okay.
It shakes like a tractor. I like it.
I didn’t tell anybody. About the gas station. Like you said.
If anybody asks, I’ll tell them how it was. You told me to.
I’ll count her breaths.

Taking his little sister to their grandma’s. And this one’s got a busted nose — got in a fight over me. Hero, right?
If they send me back there, I’m never getting out.
A little bit of everywhere. Right now — from the side of the road.
Don’t ask any more, okay? I’ll start lying and you’ll notice. You’re that kind.
You zone out sometimes. One second you’re here, the next you’re gone. I noticed.
You go to him with something wrong. You leave without it.
And without pieces of yourself. You just don’t remember which ones.
Listen. Does he really not remember what happened at home?
And you?
You asked about the bracelet, back then.
You didn’t ask about the bracelet, back then. I noticed.
No. But thanks for asking. That’s rare.
Count me out. I’m not going back in there. No way.
Oh. It’s you. Mr. “Maybe you’re right.”
Thanks for back there. In the van. People don’t usually believe me.
I saw what you did to the orderly. I’m not scared. Mostly.
I’m not great with babies. But fine. Go.

A rig jackknifed at kilometer forty-six. Right across the road. Nobody’s getting through till morning.
There’s a side road to the right, through the villages. If it doesn’t drift over.
I wouldn’t try it in a blizzard. Get stuck out in the fields and nobody’ll find you.
From the north. It’s worse up there than here.

Suits us. We’re spending the night.
The lakes froze early this year. Black ice.
Black ice is pretty. It just won’t hold you.
Hey, kid. We were watching the weather.
…Fair enough.

More tea, love?
A hundred and forty. No rush, though — the blizzard won’t let anybody out.
In winter, yes. In summer the fishermen head up to the lakes — you can’t squeeze through.
In winter it’s only this lot. And folks like you. The ones who really need to get north.

She draws well. At her age all I could do was horses.
Leave her be. We’re fine.
My belly keeps going hard. It’s nothing, it happens.
…Yes. A month.
Is he always like this — doing everything himself?
Mine decided everything himself too. For me.
I left. But I can’t throw the ring away.
A trucker gave me a ride… Said we’d get around the semi through the village. We got stuck. He went for a tractor. Ages ago.
You didn’t take me with you at the diner. And then you pulled me out of a snowdrift anyway.

…northbound highway: a jackknifed truck. The road is closed until morning.
Heavy drifts on side roads. If your car gets stuck, keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow and leave a window open.
Police are asking anyone who sees a dark sedan with one headlight…
Police are asking anyone who sees a dark sedan, license plate…

I cut him out. The year he forbade her to visit me.
Before him — yes. She sang all the time. Then she stopped.
Put it back where you found it, dear. I go through those myself.
Potatoes and pickles down there. And it’s dry. Remember it — just in case.
Sit down, dear. Those legs aren’t made of iron.
He was saving them. Said they were for a rainy day. Well, here it is.
Grandpa’s. Drove Annie to school in it, twelve versts each way. She’d belt out songs in the back the whole ride.
Who’d want it? But I need it. You sit inside — it smells of him. Shag tobacco and gasoline.
To the lake. Where else? That’s where you were headed from the start.
Well, mechanic? The sun’s already high.
Let it cool, then fix it. Grandpa always waited half an hour. Smoked.
“Quiet Pines”… That’s where I sent her. To him. To the doctor.
Well, it’s cooled off by now. We can’t stand here forever.
Walk on the white. Where it’s black — don’t step. You hear me?
Stubborn. At eight she walked to town on her own — for a kitten. Twelve versts. And she brought it home.
You take after her. Just as pigheaded.
He never throws anything away. If the truth about Annie is anywhere — it’s there.
Grandpa split them. Every summer — enough for two winters ahead.
That’s why she never told me anything. He told her not to.

Iris, sweetheart, come on out. The little one needs to get warm.
Look at the shore, Noah. Zoe’s had a lot of medication. In this cold, that’s dangerous — she needs a doctor. Come with me, and everyone goes home.
Look at the shore. Danny’s frozen stiff. Come with me, and I’ll take him to his mom.
Noah… Your hand…
Noah… Noah, please…
